5
A digital meter has an accuracy of ±1%.
The meter is used to measure the current in an electrical circuit.
The reading on the meter varies between 3.04 A and 3.08 A.
What is the value of the current, with its uncertainty?
A
(3.06 ± 0.02) A
B
(3.06 ± 0.04) A
C
(3.06 ± 0.05) A
D
(3.06 ± 0.07) A

hints: Notice the readings vary from $3.04$ $\text{A}$ to $3.08$ $\text{A}$, so find the mean value and half the range for the fluctuation uncertainty.
Connect the stated $\pm 1$% accuracy to an absolute uncertainty using $1$% of the mean current near $3.06$ $\text{A}$.
Combine the two contributions by adding the fluctuation part of about $0.02$ $\text{A}$ to the accuracy part of about $0.03$ $\text{A}$.
walkthrough: Take the best value as the mean of the extreme readings: $(3.04+3.08)/2 = 3.06$ $\text{A}$.
Find the uncertainty due to variation as half the range: $(3.08-3.04)/2 = 0.02$ $\text{A}$.
Find the uncertainty due to meter accuracy as $1$% of the reading: $0.01 \times 3.06 = 0.0306$ $\text{A}$, about $0.03$ $\text{A}$.
Add the two independent uncertainties for the total absolute uncertainty: $0.02 + 0.03 = 0.05$ $\text{A}$.
Write the result as $(3.06 \pm 0.05)$ $\text{A}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This uses only half the range $(3.08-3.04)/2 = 0.02$ $\text{A}$ and ignores the $\pm 1$% meter accuracy.

B.explanation: This uses the full range $3.08-3.04 = 0.04$ $\text{A}$ as the uncertainty and ignores the $\pm 1$% meter accuracy.

C.explanation: The mean is $3.06$ $\text{A}$ and the combined uncertainty from fluctuation $0.02$ $\text{A}$ plus $1$% accuracy $0.03$ $\text{A}$ is $0.05$ $\text{A}$.

D.explanation: This overestimates the uncertainty; $1$% of $3.06$ $\text{A}$ is about $0.03$ $\text{A}$, not $0.05$ $\text{A}$ to add to the $0.02$ $\text{A}$ fluctuation.
